title: Craft First Product Capability Vertical
objective: Carry the admitted CML-07 Craft identity foundation through one exact Product Capability vertical to candidate runtime and consumer migration evidence without collapsing Product Feature, Product Capability, Capability Instance, Bounded Context, specification, implementation, or conformance identities.

predecessor.claim_used: CML-07 is complete only at the Craft identity-contract boundary.

planning_basis.effect: Planning evidence only; the proposal is not treated as an admission or execution authorization.

interaction_profile.rule: All exact candidate bytes and collect-all receipts are authored before one human interaction. Each request retains its own owner, target, effect, and outcome. Ordered application follows the dependency graph and stops at the first failed effect.
interaction_profile.unknown_target_rule: No exact-byte request may enter the final set before its target and digest exist.

missing: canonical Realization Contract and environment-profile Definitions
current_gaps.consequence: The corresponding Artifact Types and D65 successor claims cannot yet be admitted or evaluated.

missing: Product Capability Artifact Type under Artifact Type/v2
exact Product Feature to Product Capability relation decision
current_gaps.consequence: The System Construction Product Feature and the migration proposal's first vertical cannot be silently treated as an adopted Product Capability.

missing: exact Product Capability identity and version
exact Capability Instance identity and version
Bounded Context identity or explicit no-context posture
current_gaps.consequence: No source migration or implementation slice is selected.

placement_resolution.rule: The current selected architecture places owner-local Capability Instances inside Bounded Context packages. An explicit no-context posture is valid as a semantic decision, but it cannot silently invent a directory or reuse the Product Capability definition path as the instance root.

author Product Capability adoption, business-ontology, specification, compiler-output, platform-profile, implementation-binding, and conformance owner assignments

exit_evidence: all new Artifact Types bind admitted-or-final-bundle-targeted semantic Definitions
all owner roles have non-overlapping scopes
all human projections reproduce from canonical machine records
hostile collapse fixtures fail for the intended reason

layers.theme: semantic closure and exact vertical selection
layers.minimum_working_unit: One machine-valid Product Capability candidate, one distinct Capability Instance envelope, one explicit Bounded Context or no-context posture, exact source selectors, and a recursion stop—without business ontology or implementation.
layers.visible_outcome: A reviewer can identify exactly what the first vertical is and prove that none of its identities came from naming or directory placement.
layers.risk_retired: Silent Product Feature/Product Capability collapse and migration-by-directory.
layers.costs_introduced: A deliberate semantic and owner-closure pass before source migration.
layers.exit_evidence: Definitions, Artifact Types, owners, negative fixtures, and the selected envelope are complete as exact candidates.
layers.promotion_rule: L1 may be authored only against the exact L0 candidate graph; its semantic/admission claims remain not_evaluable until the final ordered decision set applies L0 requests.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: Product Feature, Product Capability, Capability Instance, Bounded Context, and directory remain independent.

layers.minimum_working_unit: The selected capability promise, its minimal business ontology closure, and the Capability Instance binding.
layers.visible_outcome: The vertical's product promise and domain meaning are reviewable without code or runtime details.
layers.risk_retired: Importing ambient ontology material or transferring parent capability authority to its instance.
layers.costs_introduced: Explicit source admission and context-local language accounting.
layers.exit_evidence: Exact concept closure, source bindings, map ownership, and parent/instance separation checks.
layers.promotion_rule: L2 consumes only the exact L1 candidate closure; no semantic admission is inferred.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: No unselected ontology node or inferred Context Map backreference enters the vertical.

layers.theme: authored specification and deterministic system model
layers.minimum_working_unit: One authored specification that compiles twice to identical graph and system-ontology bytes.
layers.visible_outcome: The intended system model is inspectable and reproducible before any implementation choice.
layers.risk_retired: Generated output becoming a second authority or compiler drift changing meaning silently.
layers.costs_introduced: Pinned compiler identity and source-to-output trace evidence.
layers.exit_evidence: Two-run determinism plus complete authored-source, graph, and system-ontology traceability.
layers.promotion_rule: L3 binds realizations only to the exact L2 system ontology digest.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: Generated graph and system ontology remain projections of authored canonical source.

layers.theme: realization, environment, and exact implementation binding
layers.minimum_working_unit: One selected realization under a pinned environment with every system obligation mapped to an exact final-path component or typed residue.
layers.visible_outcome: A reviewer can see how the system model will be realized and reproduce the environment selection.
layers.risk_retired: Mutable global dependencies, language-driven semantic authority, and untraceable implementation scope.
layers.costs_introduced: Profile, lock, cache-policy, and binding maintenance.
layers.exit_evidence: Closed profile/lock checks and total implementation-binding coverage or explicit residue.
layers.promotion_rule: L4 materializes and exercises only exact L3 bindings.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: Profiles, installations, implementations, and conformance results stay independently identified.
layers.next_layer: L4 runtime evidence and final decision packaging

layers.theme: bounded runtime, selected consumers, rollback, and one final checkpoint
layers.minimum_working_unit: One final-path Craft vertical that installs, builds, tests, executes its bounded witness, reproduces deterministically, and rolls back without touching the legacy source.
layers.visible_outcome: Exact candidate bytes and scope-separated evidence are ready for one owner interaction.
layers.risk_retired: Broad consumer rewrites, inflated conformance claims, unrehearsed rollback, and approval of unknown bytes.
layers.costs_introduced: Independent conformance execution and a closed exact-byte decision manifest.
layers.exit_evidence: Collect-all receipts, independent scoped conformance, reproducibility, rollback, and a complete Decision Request Set.
layers.promotion_rule: Only explicit outcomes in the final request set may be applied, in dependency order; the first failed effect stops application.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: One interaction never merges authority, and publication/deployment remain separate future effects.
layers.next_layer: separate publication or stable-release workflow, only if later requested

final_decision_request_set_shape.effect: Admit exact semantic Definitions, Artifact Types, and owner-registry postimage in dependency order.
Select exact capability, instance, context posture, source closure, recursion stop, and rollback boundary.
Admit the exact capability, business ontology, authored specification, compiled graph, and system ontology.
Accept the exact implementation binding and only the named conformance scopes supported by current evidence.
Authorize only the manifest-bound local activation and selected consumer rebindings with the rehearsed rollback.

non_regression_guarantees: Machine records are canonical and human projections are generated only.
The admitted CML-07 decision and all predecessor candidates remain byte-preserved.
Craft remains the same Product lineage formerly named DomainSpec v2.
Product Feature is not Product Capability; Product Capability is not Capability Instance.
A Bounded Context exists only when semantic scope, language, owner, and contracts justify it; a directory cannot create one.
Every new Artifact Type registration uses Artifact Type/v2 and explicit semantic_definition_refs.
No D65 successor receives an admitted or conformant claim while an applicable predecessor is missing, stale, or unadmitted.
Validation, schema conformance, identity-contract conformance, construction conformance, implementation conformance, installation conformance, and runtime conformance remain distinct scopes.
One human checkpoint aggregates independently governed exact requests; it does not aggregate authority.
Git publication, release, deployment, destructive deletion, and stable-version declaration remain outside this chain.

recommended_next_unit.scope: Inventory exact CyberAlchemy-v2 meanings for the missing first-vertical terms, decide preserve/revise/split/reclassify/drop per term, then author only the dependency-closed Definition, Artifact Type, hostile-fixture, and owner candidates.
recommended_next_unit.effect_ceiling: candidate authoring and validation only; no admission, vertical selection, source copy, implementation, or runtime effect

claim_ceiling: This candidate authors the CML-08 through CML-12 dependency graph, five-layer implementation model, semantic gaps, exact output surfaces, validation obligations, and one final interaction shape only. It does not admit a Definition, Artifact Type, owner, Product Capability, Capability Instance, Bounded Context, ontology, specification, graph, implementation binding, conformance claim, runtime, migration, publication, deployment, or stable release.
